headline: Maine oil-heating bills projected to approach $3,000 this winter
dek: A new regional estimate puts the average Maine household's heating-oil cost 77% above last winter, as state data show prices above $6 a gallon and assistance applications open.
body: Maine households that heat with oil are facing a sharply more expensive winter, with the average cost projected to reach $2,939, according to a September 29 report by WMTW News 8 citing the National Energy Assistance Directors Association. The estimate is for the 2026-27 heating season and does not represent a guaranteed bill for every household.

The projected figure is 77% higher than the $1,664 comparison figure reported for last winter. WMTW said that increase is tied with Vermont for the largest projected rise among states in the Northeast. The comparison is especially significant in Maine, where heating oil remains a major household fuel and where many homes begin the heating season with little room for a large price shock.

The estimate arrived as Maine's own fuel survey showed oil prices at $6.02 per gallon. The Maine Department of Energy Resources reported that statewide average on September 21, with surveyed prices ranging from $5.00 to $6.45. The department cautions that the figures are cash prices from delivered-fuel retailers, not pre-buy or discounted contracts, and that local prices can vary considerably. Its current price page is https://www.maine.gov/energy/heating-fuel-prices.

A seasonal average is not the same as a forecast for an individual home. Actual spending will depend on the amount of oil a household uses, the size and efficiency of the building, the length and severity of the cold season, and the price charged by the local supplier. The projection also describes heating-oil users; households using propane, natural gas, wood or electricity will face different costs. Maine's energy office says its comparison dashboard is intended to show relative heating costs and does not include the cost of installing a new heating system.

The price pressure matters beyond the monthly fuel bill. A household that spends more to heat its home has less money available for rent, food, transportation and medical expenses. It can also make the timing of a delivery important: a family that delays an order while waiting for a lower price may still need fuel before the weather turns colder. Maine's Department of Energy Resources publishes a winter-heating guide and updates its delivered-fuel survey during the heating season, giving consumers a way to compare the statewide benchmark with local offers.

State assistance is available for eligible households, but it is income- and household-size based. MaineHousing says its Home Energy Assistance Program helps qualified homeowners and renters with heating costs, fuel deliveries, energy-related repairs and some utility payments. Applications for the 2026-27 HEAP season opened August 3 and continue until funds are exhausted or May 29, 2027. Details and the application are available at https://www.mainehousing.org/programs-services/Energy/energydetails/LIHEAP.

MaineHousing also says crisis assistance for households with extremely low fuel supplies will open November 1. That program requires a HEAP application first and is administered through local Community Action Agencies. The agency encourages residents to apply early, because benefits depend on eligibility and available funds. For readers trying to plan, the immediate next steps are to check the current local price, review the state's assistance rules and avoid treating the $2,939 projection as a promise that every home will spend the same amount.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Maine heating oil costs projected to hit $2,939
seoDescription: Maine heating-oil costs are projected to average $2,939 this winter as state fuel prices reach $6.02 per gallon and heating aid applications remain open.
sourceName: WMTW News 8, citing the National Energy Assistance Directors Association
